what: Agents in flight, and why. A finished agent is REMOVED from this file, not marked done — the page shows what is happening now, and history lives in git.

agents.what: Stop calling guarantees grants, and stop offering funds that are not funds
agents.why: One transposed letter in a lookup table has been recording every guarantee scheme as a grant. Italy's largest — €14.9 billion across 13,892 awards — is shown to founders as a grant, while a founder who asks for a guarantee is never shown it at all. Separately, eleven rows a founder can be offered are not funds but accounting labels: Poland's entire list is eight of them, so a Polish founder is currently shown nothing real.

agents.what: Check the founder's second answers actually reach the model that picks the five
agents.why: Step 3 asks the founder follow-up questions and step 5 is meant to use the answers. Nobody has confirmed the answers survive the trip. If they are dropped, every hour spent improving the questions is wasted; if they can rule a fund OUT, that breaks a decision already made — the second screen informs the choice, it never removes an option.

agents.what: Stop a routine sync from deleting a thousand eligibility rules
agents.why: The two ways we move the corpus between the master copy and a working copy both replace the whole file. One store currently holds about a thousand eligibility rules the other does not, so the next sync in either direction destroys them — these are the rules that decide whether a fund can rule a founder out. Making the sync refuse while that is true removes the hazard permanently.

agents.what: Get the two blind spots in the eligibility read open again
agents.why: Two checks that decide whether a rule may rule a founder out have been failing, so the ranker is working with an eligibility read we cannot vouch for. Re-running the classifiers over the rules added this week closes both, and settles whether anything published since Sunday can be trusted to exclude a founder.
